indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.1.1.1: Show understanding of the physical features and life processes of living things and use this understanding to classify them
indicator.objective: Observe and describe different kinds of things in the environment.

skills.description: Observe and name things found in the immediate environment
Describe observable features of a named thing
Group observed things by simple observable criteria

misconceptions: Only animals are living things; plants are not living.
Things in the environment are only what we can see inside the classroom.

questions.stem: What is the name of the thing in the sky that gives us light during the day?
hints: Look up during the day.
It is very bright and yellow.
questions.explanation: The sun is the bright object in the sky during the day. It gives us light and warmth.
questions.misconception: Some pupils think the moon gives light during the day, but the moon is mainly seen at night.

questions.stem: Which of these things can you find in a classroom?
hints: Think about what you sit at in school.
It is made of wood.
questions.explanation: A desk is a piece of furniture found in a classroom. Cars, rivers, and goats are found outside.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name things from home or outside instead of focusing on the classroom.

questions.stem: Name one thing you can see in your school compound.
hints: Look outside your classroom.
It can be a plant or an object.
questions.explanation: There are many things in the school compound, such as trees, grass, stones, or the school building.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name things inside the classroom instead of the compound.

questions.stem: Which is a thing you see in a market?
hints: Think about where people buy food.
It is a red food item.
questions.explanation: Tomatoes are sold in markets. Blackboards are for schools, and beds are for homes.
questions.misconception: Pupils might choose blackboard because it is a familiar object, but it is not found in a market.

questions.stem: Which of these is found in the sky at night?
hints: Think about when it is dark.
It is round and shines at night.
questions.explanation: The moon is seen in the sky at night. The sun is seen during the day.
questions.misconception: Pupils may choose the sun, forgetting that the sun is for the day.

questions.stem: A stone is usually...
hints: Touch a stone.
It is not soft like a pillow.
questions.explanation: A stone is hard. It does not bend or flow like water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the hardness of a stone with other properties.

questions.stem: How would you describe the colour of a typical leaf?
hints: Look at a plant.
It is the colour of grass.
questions.explanation: Most healthy leaves are green.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all leaves are the same colour as flowers.

questions.stem: Adwoa sees a mango. How can she describe its shape?
hints: Think about the shape of a ball.
It is not flat like paper.
questions.explanation: A mango is round in shape.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse shape with other features like size or colour.

questions.stem: Describe one thing about a goat.
hints: Think about what a goat looks like.
Does it have horns or wings?
questions.explanation: A goat has four legs, horns, and eats grass. These are observable features.
questions.misconception: Pupils may describe what a goat does instead of what it looks like.

questions.stem: Look at a pencil and a piece of paper. Describe how they are different in colour and how they feel.

criteria.description: States a correct colour difference (e.g., pencil is yellow/wood, paper is white)
States a correct difference in how they feel (e.g., pencil is hard, paper is soft/smooth)

hints: Look at the colours.
Touch them gently. Which is harder?
questions.explanation: This requires observation and description of two features.

questions.stem: We can put things into groups. Which group does a chair belong to?
hints: Think about what you sit on.
It is not something you eat.
questions.explanation: A chair is furniture. It is used for sitting.
questions.misconception: Pupils may group items by where they are found instead of what they are.

questions.stem: Kwame has a cup, a plate, and a spoon. What group can they all belong to?
hints: Think about what you do with them.
They are used in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: A cup, plate, and spoon are all used when eating or drinking.
questions.misconception: Pupils may group them by material or colour instead of their use.

questions.stem: Sort these into two groups: dog, cat, stone, chair.
answer: living: dog cat, non-living: stone chair
animals: dog cat, objects: stone chair
hints: Which ones can move and grow?
Which ones cannot?
questions.explanation: Dogs and cats are living things (animals). Stones and chairs are non-living things.
questions.misconception: Pupils may struggle to find the common criteria for grouping.

questions.stem: Where would you find fish?
hints: Think about where fish swim.
They need water to live.
questions.explanation: Fish live in water. They need water to breathe and swim.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fish can live anywhere like land animals.

questions.stem: Which of these words describes a balloon?
hints: Think about the shape of a ball.
It can hold air.
questions.explanation: A blown-up balloon is round. It is not square or flat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think of a deflated balloon which is flat.

questions.stem: Ama found an object. It is round, small, and used to buy things. What is it?
hints: Think about money.
It is made of metal.
questions.explanation: A coin is round, small, and used as money to buy things.
questions.misconception: Pupils may choose another round object like a stone, ignoring the clue about buying things.

questions.stem: Why do we put a dog and a cat in the same group?
hints: Think about what they are.
They both have fur and breathe.
questions.explanation: A dog and a cat are both animals. They share features like moving, breathing, and eating.
questions.misconception: Pupils may group them by size or colour instead of fundamental characteristics.

questions.stem: Draw a tree and a stone. Write one word to describe the tree and one word to describe the stone.

criteria.description: Uses a correct describing word for the tree (e.g., tall, green)
Uses a correct describing word for the stone (e.g., hard, grey)

hints: What does a tree look like?
How does a stone feel?
questions.explanation: This tests observation, drawing, and description.

questions.stem: Tell me three things you can see outside the window right now.

criteria.description: Names a second correct object outside
Names a third correct object outside

hints: Look carefully.
Name what you see on the ground or in the sky.
questions.explanation: This tests real-time observation skills.

questions.stem: Which of these does NOT belong with the others?
hints: Think about what you can eat.
One of these is not a fruit.
questions.explanation: Mango, orange, and banana are fruits. A stone is not a fruit.
questions.misconception: Pupils may sort by colour instead of category.
